newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey teens accused of killing their baby.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey teens accused of killing their baby.

text.p: Two college freshmen have been accused of murdering their newborn baby and could face the death penalty, authorities said on Monday.

Police say Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson, both 18, murdered the baby boy after Grossberg gave birth last week in a motel room in Delaware. They are accused of hitting the baby in the head and stuffing him into a plastic bag, which they dumped in a trash can before dawn last Tuesday.

The body was found the next day and an autopsy showed the baby died of severe skull fractures. The motel was just a few miles from the University of Delaware, where Grossberg is a freshman. Peterson, who helped with the baby's delivery, is a freshman at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania.

The two are charged with first-degree murder and could face the death penalty, Delaware Deputy Attorney General Peter Letang said on Monday. They would be the youngest people to face capital punishment in the state, he said.
Letang said Grossberg was in a Delaware hospital because of complications from the childbirth and Peterson was with his family on Monday and was expected to turn himself in to authorities.

"We are confused," said Seth Chorba, 18 a freshman from Trenton, New Jersey, who lives in the dorm with Grossberg. "She is just a great person. She was always smiling. You couldn't have made up a story like this because no one would have believed you."
The case also shocked neighbours and friends in the affluent New Jersey towns of Franklin Lakes, where Grossberg grew up, and nearby Wyckoff, where Peterson had lived.
"They are both great kids," said one of Peterson's neighbours. "You could call them an ideal young couple. Both were smart and friendly. And they seemed so happy."
